prompt:
Create a realistic production-quality editorial WEBSITE design for Missional by Design, edge to edge, 1440 pixels wide by 2000 pixels tall, showing a continuous homepage and several sections. Crisp readable UI text, no browser or device frame, no concept labels. Audience: Christian technologists and ministry/product leaders. The offer connects Christian purpose, changing context and practical design. Preserve the approved rock specimen from reference image 1: the same broad fractured outline and reflective pale icy blue-silver faces. No new rock silhouette, dents, tiny gravel texture, glass crystal, physical cross cutout or biblical props. A sharp four-point optical reflection with slight local glow is part of this identity. Reference images 2 and 3 are quality benchmarks for confident hierarchy, human photography and editorial rhythm, not brands/layouts to copy. Reference image 4 provides an approved fictional startup working scene. Use no fabricated testimonials, endorsements or performance statistics. Small captions identify generated editorial imagery. At most two type families; readable body type, restrained structural devices, no repetitive cards, excessive labels or large black slabs. One primary action. Navigation reads Principles, Canvas, Patterns, Writing, About, EN / DE. Wordmark: missional — by — design, with two short rules around by. Show real text in every visible section. Current date is 16 October 2026; no dates are needed.
Art direction: a luminous contemporary identity centred on reflected light, with a pale ice-blue atmosphere, dark blue ink, restrained optical highlights and a beautiful large serif used as an active editorial voice. The approved rock is the one memorable object in the opening: isolate that same specimen from reference 1 on the page surface, preserving its physical silhouette, pale-blue fractured mirror faces and glint. A spatial, gallery-like composition integrates the large headline around generous negative space; avoid a standard split hero or a centred headline above three cards. Headline: “What really is good news here?” Deck: “Christian reflection and practical tools for a changing context.” Primary action: “Find your starting point”. Include a short human startup-photo band from reference 4 early in the flow so this is a human resource, not a luxury metal brand. Below, present an inviting worked design question: “A missed day. A welcoming return.” One sentence: “Explore how a reading app can help someone begin again.” Show a modest clearly labelled design-example preview, no fake data, linked to “Compare the options”. Follow with an editorial set of clear routes “Principles”, “Canvas”, “Patterns”, each with a short purposeful description. The continuous page should show varied scale and density while retaining a calm, highly readable system. No physical cross motif; the optical glint remains subtle.
Use people and photographs ONLY from reference 4 or new fictional people; never copy faces or photographs from the two comparator screenshots. They are craft references only.
